title: Characterizing Inhibition of SARS-CoV-2 Infection by a Protein in Cultured Cells

steps.title: Prepare MUC1 stock solution
steps.instruction: Centrifuge the lyophilized MUC1 vial at 10,000 × g for 1 min before opening. Dissolve the protein in PBS containing 5 % trehalose (pH 7.2) to a final concentration of 0.1 mg/mL. Do not vortex or pipette mix. Store the stock at 4 °C for up to 1 week or aliquot and keep at –80 °C for up to 3 months, avoiding repeated freeze‑thaw cycles.

steps.title: Thaw and plate Caco-2-N cells
steps.instruction: Rapidly thaw one vial of Caco-2‑N cells in a 37 °C water bath and immediately seed the cells into a 10 cm cell‑culture dish.

steps.title: Culture Caco-2-N cells
steps.instruction: Grow the cells in Basic DMEM (high glucose, pyruvate) supplemented with 1 % Streptomycin/Penicillin and 10 % fetal bovine serum at 37 °C, 5 % CO₂. Split the cultures twice per week at a 1:6 ratio; for larger scale, transfer to a 175 cm² Corning TC‑treated flask (cat# 431080). Maintain the cells for at least 5–7 days after thawing before infection.

steps.title: Harvest cells and extract total RNA
steps.instruction: Collect the culture supernatant and add 250 µL sterile PBS to wash the adherent cells. Aspirate the PBS, then add 250 µL Buffer RL1 (containing 1 % v/v β‑mercaptoethanol) to lyse the cells. Transfer the lysate to a 1.7 mL RNase‑free microcentrifuge tube. Add Buffer RL2, Buffer RW1, Buffer RW2 and 100 µL RNase‑free ddH₂O according to the FastPure Cell/Tissue Total RNA Isolation Kit (Vazyme) protocol (or an equivalent kit) to purify total RNA.

steps.title: Synthesize first‑strand cDNA
steps.instruction: In a sterile 0.2 mL PCR tube on ice, combine 11 µL RNA template with 1 µL Random Hexamer primer, mix gently, centrifuge briefly, and incubate at 65 °C for 5 min. Chill on ice, spin down, and keep on ice. Prepare a premix (1.2× the required volume) containing 2× Reaction Buffer, RNase Inhibitor (20 U/µL), 10 mM dNTP Mix, and RevertAid M‑MuLV Reverse Transcriptase (200 U/µL) to a total of 8 µL per reaction. Add 8 µL premix to each tube, mix gently, and incubate 5 min at 25 °C, 60 min at 42 °C, then terminate the reaction by heating at 70 °C for 5 min.

steps.title: Set up qPCR reactions
steps.instruction: For each 96‑well reaction prepare 5 µL 2× PowerUp™ SYBR Green Master Mix, 1 µL forward primer (10 µM), 1 µL reverse primer (10 µM), and 3 µL cDNA template (total 10 µL). Primer sequences: SARS‑CoV‑2‑RNA‑F 5′‑CGAAAGGTAAGATGGAGAGCC‑3′, SARS‑CoV‑2‑RNA‑R 5′‑TGTTGACGTGCCTCTGATAAG‑3′, RPS11‑F 5′‑GCCGAGACTATCTGCACTAC‑3′, RPS11‑R 5′‑ATGTCCAGCCTCAGAACTTC‑3′. Optionally make a 1.2× premix of Master Mix and primers to compensate for pipetting loss. Mix thoroughly, centrifuge briefly, dispense the reaction mix into an optical 96‑well plate, seal with a MicroAmp™ Optical Adhesive Film, and centrifuge again to remove bubbles.

steps.title: Run qRT‑PCR thermal program
steps.instruction: Place the sealed plate in the qRT‑PCR instrument and run the following cycling protocol: UDG activation 50 °C 2 min; Dual‑Lock™ DNA polymerase activation 95 °C 20 s; Denature 95 °C 3 s; Anneal/extend 60 °C 35 s (40 cycles). Perform a dissociation curve: 95 °C 15 s, 60 °C 20 s, 95 °C 15 s, 60 °C 15 s.

steps.title: Analyze infection ratio and inhibition
steps.instruction: Calculate the relative viral RNA expression using the RPS11 housekeeping gene for normalization. Compare the values from MUC1‑treated samples to the negative control to determine the infection ratio and inhibition percentage. In the referenced experiment, MUC1 showed strong inhibition of SARS‑CoV‑2 infection.

description: The protocol below describes detailed procedures for researchers to investigate the ability of a protein of interest to inhibit SARS-CoV-2 infection in a transcription and replication-competent SARS-CoV-2 virus-like particles lacking nucleocapsid (N) gene (SARS-CoV-2 ΔN trVLP) infection system. Meanwhile, breast milk inhibits several viral infections, such as human immunodeficiency virus (HIV), cytomegalovirus (CMV), dengue virus, rotavirus, enterovirus, and adenovirus (Kell et al., 2020; van der Strate et al., 2001). Here we evaluate the antiviral effect of a protein of interest using human breast milk component of mucin1 (MUC1) as an example in a cell infection system of SARS-CoV-2 ΔN trVLP infecting Caco-2-N cells to mimic authentic SARS-CoV-2 infection (Lai et al., 2022; Ju et al., 2021).Note: Caco-2 are epithelial cells isolated from colon tissue derived from a 72-year-old, white, male patient with colorectal adenocarcinoma (ATCC HTB-37™, https://www.atcc.org/products/htb-37). Caco-2-N cells are established to stably express SARS-CoV-2 N protein by lentiviral transduction. The reason why we choose Caco-2 as infection cell model is that Caco-2 cells express high level of SARS-CoV-2 receptors of ACE2 and TMPRSS2, which are permissive to SARS-CoV-2. Caco-2 cells were widely used to study infection with SARS-CoV and are now again being used to study SARS-CoV2 infections (Bojkova et al., 2020).Note: SARS-CoV-2 ΔN trVLP expresses a reporter gene (green fluorescent protein, GFP) replacing viral nucleocapsid gene (N), which is required for viral genome packaging and virion assembly. The lack of the viral N protein could be genetically complemented in trans by ectopic expression in Caco-2-N cells. SARS-CoV-2 ΔN trVLP could be propagated and passaged in Caco-2-N cells. If you would like to know more details about the Caco-2-N production, trVLP production and viral titration, you are highly recommended to refer to another published detailed protocol well-written by Prof.
